Subject: Design review: internal SSL proxy routing and cert handoff for private deploy

Hi all,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Per our onboarding with Sable Finance, there are three viable approaches for TLS termination and certificate management in their private VPC/on-prem deployment and we need to pick a primary and fallback that meet their compliance constraints (no ACME to public endpoints, monthly rotation, mutual auth for control-plane).

Options summary (quick):
- Option A: Customer edge terminates TLS (preferred by security) and we connect over a mutually authenticated mTLS tunnel to a private Redwood control plane endpoint. Customer supplies certs; Redwood validates client certs.
- Option B: Redwood terminates at a private NLB + Envoy inside the VPC (Redwood-managed certs stored in KMS/HSM). Use internal CA brokering with the customer providing root trust anchor.
- Option C: Transparent TCP pass-through to customer LB; Redwood does no termination (lowest surface area) but loses ability to do prefix/KV caching and request-level routing.

Key constraints from Sable:
- Must enforce client certificate authentication for any control-plane traffic.
- No public ACME; certs must be handed off through a secured artifact exchange (SFTP/Hash-signed bundle) or uploaded into their vault and cross-trusted.
- Audit logs and rotation timeline: rotation every 30 days, with overlap window of 7 days.

Attachments: internal-ssl-proxy-certflow-diagram.svg (diagram), mtls-handoff-checklist.pdf (checklist), customer-cert-handoff-playbook.md (playbook).

Ask: Hiro/Grace/Karthik — can you review the diagram and checklist and flag any operational gaps? I'm scheduling a call with Sable security on Monday to lock the approach.

Thanks,
--

Thanks Monica — diagram looks solid. A couple operational notes from the runtime side: 

1) If we terminate at a private Envoy in the VPC (Option B), we must ensure our KV cache prefixing preserves end-to-end auth semantics. That means we cannot cache request payloads unless the client's cert binds the session (we can store per-client-prefix cache keys).

2) For Option A (customer terminates), we'll need a lightweight agent or a tunneled control-plane protocol to carry per-request metadata (trace id, routing hints). Otherwise we lose per-request routing and quality controls.

3) Cert rotation automation: we should support both push (customer uploads new cert to our onboarding SFTP + API) and pull (we hit a customer PKI endpoint over an authenticated channel). Either way, verify fingerprint on ingestion and log to audit stream.

Operational gap I see in the checklist: add a step to verify CRL/OCSP reachability from inside the customer's VPC for any certs we rely on.

-Hiro
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Agree with Hiro. From a security/compliance perspective I'm inclined to recommend Option A as default for Sable given their audit constraints — customer-managed termination + mTLS to our control plane. That minimizes Redwood's handling of private cert material and aligns with their SOC/PCI needs.

Trade-offs to call out to Sable:
- We will request permission to run a lightweight tunnel endpoint inside their VPC to capture request-level metadata for observability and quality checks. This agent will only see headers/traces and will not store raw payloads.
- If they insist on absolute zero termination inside their perimeter, we'll limit feature set (no per-token caching, limited streaming optimizations).

I'll add the CRL/OCSP step Hiro mentioned and a section on acceptable artifact exchange methods (SFTP signed bundle, vendor-signed zip, HashiCorp Vault cross-entry).

-Grace

Couple of additions on the brokering model (Option B variant):

- Internal CA brokering: We can run an intermediate CA inside Redwood KMS and issue short-lived leaf certs that are cross-signed by the customer's root. Customer provides the root CA cert once via a secure channel. This lets Redwood manage rotation internally while the customer retains a root-of-trust.

- HSM integration: if Sable requires, we can store private keys in a FIPS 140-2 HSM object and require HSM-signed CSR flows. That will add latency to rotation but meets higher assurance levels.

- DNS: split-horizon preferred. Create an internal DNS zone for redwood-private.sable.internal pointing to our private endpoints. We should provide an IaC snippet (Terraform) to instantiate the records in the customer's private zone; avoid relying on cross-account route53 delegation unless absolutely necessary.

I'll draft the Terraform snippet and the CA brochure before the Monday sync.

-Karthik

Thanks for the options and checks. A couple constraints from our side that will determine the decision: 

- We require mutual TLS for all control-plane connections and a per-client certificate mapping. We cannot accept any wildcard SANs for control-plane certs — must be explicit CN/SAN entries.
- We do not allow remote ACME challenges from any third-party service. All cert issuance will happen from our internal PKI and pushed to vendors via signed bundles.
- Rotation cadence is monthly; we will provide overlapping certs with a 10-day overlap window.

We lean toward Option A (customer termination + mTLS) but can accept Option B if Redwood can guarantee HSM-backed key material, explicit CN/SAN issuance, and a documented audit trail for certificate issuance and revocation. Please include a checklist item for how Redwood will handle emergency revocation and notification.

We will review the diagram and checklist; please send the Terraform snippet and CA brokering brochure prior to the call.

Regards,
Chris Mills
Senior SRE, Sable Finance (FastBank)
